sanskrit: sa̱mā̱nam u̱ tyam pu̍ruhū̱tam u̱kthya1̱̍ṁ ratha̍ṁ trica̱kraṁ sava̍nā̱ gani̍gmatam | pari̍jmānaṁ vida̱thya̍ṁ suvṛ̱ktibhi̍r va̱yaṁ vyu̍ṣṭā u̱ṣaso̍ havāmahe ||
english: With well-fashioned hymns we call at the break of dawn that same much-invoked, laudable, three-wheeled chariot that comes to every soma-pressing — the wide-ranging, assembly-worthy car of the Aśvins.

sanskrit: prā̱ta̱ryuja̍ṁ nāsa̱tyādhi̍ tiṣṭhathaḥ prāta̱ryāvā̍ṇam madhu̱vāha̍na̱ṁ ratha̍m | viśo̱ yena̱ gaccha̍tho̱ yajva̍rīr narā kī̱reś ci̍d ya̱jñaṁ hotṛ̍mantam aśvinā ||
english: O Nāsatyās, ye two mount the chariot that is yoked at dawn, that goes forth at dawn, that carries sweet gifts. With it ye visit the sacrificing clans, O heroes; even the poet's sacrifice which has its Hotṛ — ye, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: a̱dhva̱ryuṁ vā̱ madhu̍pāṇiṁ su̱hastya̍m a̱gnidha̍ṁ vā dhṛ̱tada̍kṣa̱ṁ damū̍nasam | vipra̍sya vā̱ yat sava̍nāni̱ gaccha̱tho 'ta̱ ā yā̍tam madhu̱peya̍m aśvinā ||
english: Whether ye come to the Adhvaryu who holds sweets in his dexterous hand, or to the Āgnīdhra who is of firm skill and devoted to the house, or to the soma-pressings of the inspired priest — come thence, O Aśvins, to drink the honey-offering.

sanskrit: aste̍va̱ su pra̍ta̱raṁ lāya̱m asya̱n bhūṣa̍nn iva̱ pra bha̍rā̱ stoma̍m asmai | vā̱cā vi̍prās tarata̱ vāca̍m a̱ryo ni rā̍maya jaritar jā̱ram indra̍m ||
english: Like a bowman shooting his arrow farther and farther, bring forward the hymn of praise for him as if adorning him. O inspired singers, with your voice surpass the voice of the stranger; O singer, appease Indra who is swift to respond.

sanskrit: dohe̍na̱ gām upa̍ śikṣā̱ sakhā̍ya̱m pra bo̍dhaya jaritar jā̱ram indra̍m | kośa̱ṁ na pū̱rṇaṁ vasu̍nā̱ nyṛ̍ṣṭa̱m ā cyā̍vaya magha̱deyā̍ya̱ śūra̍m ||
english: Assist your friend with the milk-gift; O singer, rouse the eager Indra. Stir the hero to bestow his wealth, as one shakes a full vessel brimming over with riches.

sanskrit: kim a̱ṅga tvā̍ maghavan bho̱jam ā̍huḥ śiśī̱hi mā̍ śiśa̱yaṁ tvā̍ śṛṇomi | apna̍svatī̱ mama̱ dhīr a̍stu śakra vasu̱vida̱m bhaga̍m i̱ndrā bha̍rā naḥ ||
english: What then, O Maghavan, do they call thee the liberal giver? Sharpen me — I hear that thou art sharp already. May my prayer be rich in bounty, O Śakra; bring us, O Indra, a fortune rich in goods.

sanskrit: tvāṁ janā̍ mamasa̱tyeṣv i̍ndra saṁtasthā̱nā vi hva̍yante samī̱ke | atrā̱ yuja̍ṁ kṛṇute̱ yo ha̱viṣmā̱n nāsu̍nvatā sa̱khyaṁ va̍ṣṭi̱ śūra̍ḥ ||
english: People who have gathered in places of real conflict call on thee, O Indra, in battle. There the man who has oblations makes a comrade; the hero desires no friendship with one who does not press soma.

sanskrit: dhana̱ṁ na sya̱ndram ba̍hu̱laṁ yo a̍smai tī̱vrān somā̍m̐ āsu̱noti̱ praya̍svān | tasmai̱ śatrū̍n su̱tukā̍n prā̱tar ahno̱ ni svaṣṭrā̍n yu̱vati̱ hanti̍ vṛ̱tram ||
english: For him who presses the sharp soma-juices for Indra with oblations, bestowing abundant flowing wealth — for such a one, at the early hour of day, [Indra] slays Vṛtra and crushes the nimble foes with his well-wrought weapon.

sanskrit: yasmi̍n va̱yaṁ da̍dhi̱mā śaṁsa̱m indre̱ yaḥ śi̱śrāya̍ ma̱ghavā̱ kāma̍m a̱sme | ā̱rāc ci̱t san bha̍yatām asya̱ śatru̱r ny a̍smai dyu̱mnā janyā̍ namantām ||
english: In Indra in whom we have placed our hope, who the Bounteous One has fixed his desire upon us — may even the distant foe tremble before him; may the peoples bow down their glories to him.

sanskrit: ā̱rāc chatru̱m apa̍ bādhasva dū̱ram u̱gro yaḥ śamba̍ḥ puruhūta̱ tena̍ | a̱sme dhe̍hi̱ yava̍ma̱d goma̍d indra kṛ̱dhī dhiya̍ṁ jari̱tre vāja̍ratnām ||
english: Drive far away the hostile obstructor, O mighty one, O much-invoked; with that power keep him at a distance. Bestow on us, O Indra, riches with barley and with cattle; make our prayer prize-winning for the singer.

sanskrit: pra yam a̱ntar vṛ̍ṣasa̱vāso̱ agma̍n tī̱vrāḥ somā̍ bahu̱lāntā̍sa̱ indra̍m | nāha̍ dā̱māna̍m ma̱ghavā̱ ni ya̍ṁsa̱n ni su̍nva̱te va̍hati̱ bhūri̍ vā̱mam ||
english: When the sharp, copious soma-draughts pressed at the bull-pressings have entered Indra within — the Bounteous One never restrains his gift; to the presser he brings abundant wealth.

sanskrit: u̱ta pra̱hām a̍ti̱dīvyā̍ jayāti kṛ̱taṁ yac chva̱ghnī vi̍ci̱noti̍ kā̱le | yo de̱vakā̍mo̱ na dhanā̍ ruṇaddhi̱ sam it taṁ rā̱yā sṛ̍jati sva̱dhāvā̍n ||
english: One also wins a great stake by playing better at dice — when the dog-slaying gambler picks out the winning throw at the right moment. One who is devoted to the gods and does not withhold his wealth — him the self-powerful one unites with riches.

sanskrit: gobhi̍ṣ ṭare̱māma̍tiṁ du̱revā̱ṁ yave̍na̱ kṣudha̍m puruhūta̱ viśvā̍m | va̱yaṁ rāja̍bhiḥ pratha̱mā dhanā̍ny a̱smāke̍na vṛ̱jane̍nā jayema ||
english: With cattle may we overcome the niggardly one who is hard to approach, and with barley overcome all hunger, O much-invoked. May we, with kings, be first to win riches, with our own community winning.

sanskrit: bṛha̱spati̍r na̱ḥ pari̍ pātu pa̱ścād u̱totta̍rasmā̱d adha̍rād aghā̱yoḥ | indra̍ḥ pu̱rastā̍d u̱ta ma̍dhya̱to na̱ḥ sakhā̱ sakhi̍bhyo̱ vari̍vaḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind and from above, from below, and from the evil-doer. May Indra in front and from the midst of us, as friend to friends, make wide space for us.

sanskrit: acchā̍ ma̱ indra̍m ma̱taya̍ḥ sva̱rvida̍ḥ sa̱dhrīcī̱r viśvā̍ uśa̱tīr a̍nūṣata | pari̍ ṣvajante̱ jana̍yo̱ yathā̱ pati̱m marya̱ṁ na śu̱ndhyum ma̱ghavā̍nam ū̱taye̍ ||
english: My thoughts, all finding the sun, all yearning, together sang forth toward Indra. They embrace [him] as wives embrace their husband — the Bountiful One, pure as a young man, for our aid.

sanskrit: na ghā̍ tva̱drig apa̍ veti me̱ mana̱s tve it kāma̍m puruhūta śiśraya | rāje̍va dasma̱ ni ṣa̱do 'dhi̍ ba̱rhiṣy a̱smin su some̍ 'va̱pāna̍m astu te ||
english: Indeed my mind does not turn away from thee — upon thee alone do I fix my desire, O much-invoked. O wondrous Indra, sit down upon the sacred grass as a king; let there be a good draught for thee at this soma.

sanskrit: vi̱ṣū̱vṛd indro̱ ama̍ter u̱ta kṣu̱dhaḥ sa id rā̱yo ma̱ghavā̱ vasva̍ īśate | tasyed i̱me pra̍va̱ṇe sa̱pta sindha̍vo̱ vayo̍ vardhanti vṛṣa̱bhasya̍ śu̱ṣmiṇa̍ḥ ||
english: Indra is the dispeller of both folly and of hunger; he, the Bountiful One, is master of riches and of goods. To him the seven rivers on their downward slope increase the strength of the mighty bull.

sanskrit: vayo̱ na vṛ̱kṣaṁ su̍palā̱śam āsa̍da̱n somā̍sa̱ indra̍m ma̱ndina̍ś camū̱ṣada̍ḥ | praiṣā̱m anī̍ka̱ṁ śava̍sā̱ davi̍dyutad vi̱dat sva1̱̍r mana̍ve̱ jyoti̱r ārya̍m ||
english: Like birds settling on a fair-leafed tree, the gladdening soma-draughts settled upon Indra, dwelling in the soma-vessels. Shining forth on their band with might, he found the sun, the noble light for Manu.

sanskrit: kṛ̱taṁ na śva̱ghnī vi ci̍noti̱ deva̍ne sa̱ṁvarga̱ṁ yan ma̱ghavā̱ sūrya̱ṁ jaya̍t | na tat te̍ a̱nyo anu̍ vī̱rya̍ṁ śaka̱n na pu̍rā̱ṇo ma̍ghava̱n nota nūta̍naḥ ||
english: As a dog-slaying gambler picks out the winning throw in the game — thus [was] the conquest when the Bountiful One won the sun. No other could match that heroic deed of thine, O Maghavan — neither one of old nor one of recent times.

sanskrit: viśa̍ṁ-viśam ma̱ghavā̱ pary a̍śāyata̱ janā̍nā̱ṁ dhenā̍ ava̱cāka̍śa̱d vṛṣā̍ | yasyāha̍ śa̱kraḥ sava̍neṣu̱ raṇya̍ti̱ sa tī̱vraiḥ somai̍ḥ sahate pṛtanya̱taḥ ||
english: The Bountiful One has lain around every clan; the bull has made the song of the peoples glisten. He at whose soma-pressings Śakra takes delight — that one conquers with the sharp soma-draughts those who attack.

sanskrit: āpo̱ na sindhu̍m a̱bhi yat sa̱makṣa̍ra̱n somā̍sa̱ indra̍ṁ ku̱lyā i̍va hra̱dam | vardha̍nti̱ viprā̱ maho̍ asya̱ sāda̍ne̱ yava̱ṁ na vṛ̱ṣṭir di̱vyena̱ dānu̍nā ||
english: When the soma-juices flowed together toward Indra like waters to a river, like channels to a lake, the inspired poets strengthen his greatness at his seat, like rain [strengthens] barley with its heavenly gift.

sanskrit: vṛṣā̱ na kru̱ddhaḥ pa̍taya̱d raja̱ḥsv ā yo a̱ryapa̍tnī̱r akṛ̍ṇod i̱mā a̱paḥ | sa su̍nva̱te ma̱ghavā̍ jī̱radā̍na̱ve 'vi̍nda̱j jyoti̱r mana̍ve ha̱viṣma̍te ||
english: Like an angry bull he swept into the dust-clouds — he who made these waters subservient to noble masters. He, the Bountiful One, found the light for the swift-giving presser, for the oblation-offering Manu.

sanskrit: uj jā̍yatām para̱śur jyoti̍ṣā sa̱ha bhū̱yā ṛ̱tasya̍ su̱dughā̍ purāṇa̱vat | vi ro̍catām aru̱ṣo bhā̱nunā̱ śuci̱ḥ sva1̱̍r ṇa śu̱kraṁ śu̍śucīta̱ satpa̍tiḥ ||
english: Let the axe rise together with the light; may it be a good milch-cow of truth as in ancient times. May the bright red one shine forth with his radiance, pure as the sun; may the lord of the good blaze with brilliant light.

sanskrit: gobhi̍ṣ ṭare̱māma̍tiṁ du̱revā̱ṁ yave̍na̱ kṣudha̍m puruhūta̱ viśvā̍m | va̱yaṁ rāja̍bhiḥ pratha̱mā dhanā̍ny a̱smāke̍na vṛ̱jane̍nā jayema ||
english: With cattle may we overcome the niggardly one who is hard to approach, and with barley overcome all hunger, O much-invoked. May we, with kings, be first to win riches, with our own community winning.

sanskrit: bṛha̱spati̍r na̱ḥ pari̍ pātu pa̱ścād u̱totta̍rasmā̱d adha̍rād aghā̱yoḥ | indra̍ḥ pu̱rastā̍d u̱ta ma̍dhya̱to na̱ḥ sakhā̱ sakhi̍bhyo̱ vari̍vaḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind and from above, from below, and from the evil-doer. May Indra in front and from the midst of us, as friend to friends, make wide space for us.

sanskrit: ā yā̱tv indra̱ḥ svapa̍ti̱r madā̍ya̱ yo dharma̍ṇā tūtujā̱nas tuvi̍ṣmān | pra̱tva̱kṣā̱ṇo ati̱ viśvā̱ sahā̍ṁsy apā̱reṇa̍ maha̱tā vṛṣṇye̍na ||
english: Let Indra, the good lord, come for our exhilaration — he who is mighty, ever hastening by his sacred ordinance, swelling with overwhelming might, surpassing all resistances with his boundless, great virile power.

sanskrit: su̱ṣṭhāmā̱ ratha̍ḥ su̱yamā̱ harī̍ te mi̱myakṣa̱ vajro̍ nṛpate̱ gabha̍stau | śībha̍ṁ rājan su̱pathā yā̍hy a̱rvāṅ vardhā̍ma te pa̱puṣo̱ vṛṣṇyā̍ni ||
english: Thy chariot is well-poised, thy two bay horses well-reined; the bolt is fixed in thy fist, O lord of men. Come quickly, O king, by the good path hither — we would strengthen the virile powers thou hast drunk in.

sanskrit: endra̱vāho̍ nṛ̱pati̱ṁ vajra̍bāhum u̱gram u̱grāsa̍s tavi̱ṣāsa̍ enam | pratva̍kṣasaṁ vṛṣa̱bhaṁ sa̱tyaśu̍ṣma̱m em a̍sma̱trā sa̍dha̱mādo̍ vahantu ||
english: Let the Indra-bearers — the fierce, mighty, powerful ones — bring hither the lord of men, the bolt-armed, terrible one, the waxing bull of true force, to rejoice together here with us.

sanskrit: e̱vā pati̍ṁ droṇa̱sāca̱ṁ sace̍tasam ū̱rjaḥ ska̱mbhaṁ dha̱ruṇa̱ ā vṛ̍ṣāyase | oja̍ḥ kṛṣva̱ saṁ gṛ̍bhāya̱ tve apy aso̱ yathā̍ keni̱pānā̍m i̱no vṛ̱dhe ||
english: Thus, O lord of the press-vat, O like-minded one, thou art the bull in the steadfast pillar of strength. Exert thy power, take it into thyself, so that thou mayest be lord for the growth of those who drink of the soma.

sanskrit: gama̍nn a̱sme vasū̱ny ā hi śaṁsi̍ṣaṁ svā̱śiṣa̱m bhara̱m ā yā̍hi so̱mina̍ḥ | tvam ī̍śiṣe̱ sāsminn ā sa̍tsi ba̱rhiṣy a̍nādhṛ̱ṣyā tava̱ pātrā̍ṇi̱ dharma̍ṇā ||
english: Come to us, for riches may come our way — I have praised a self-willed gift; come, O soma-drinker, hither. Thou art the master; sit here upon the sacred grass. Thy vessels are inviolable by thy sacred order.

sanskrit: pṛtha̱k prāya̍n pratha̱mā de̱vahū̍ta̱yo 'kṛ̍ṇvata śrava̱syā̍ni du̱ṣṭarā̍ | na ye śe̱kur ya̱jñiyā̱ṁ nāva̍m ā̱ruha̍m ī̱rmaiva te ny a̍viśanta̱ kepa̍yaḥ ||
english: The earliest invocations of the gods, going separately, achieved renown hard to surpass. Those who were unable to board the sacrificial ship — those wavy fools descended only into the current itself.

sanskrit: e̱vaivāpā̱g apa̍re santu dū̱ḍhyo 'śvā̱ yeṣā̍ṁ du̱ryuja̍ āyuyu̱jre | i̱tthā ye prāg upa̍re̱ santi̍ dā̱vane̍ pu̱rūṇi̱ yatra̍ va̱yunā̍ni̱ bhoja̍nā ||
english: Thus let the others — whose horses have been yoked in a faulty manner — be turned away and be hard to milk. Those who thus are ahead and ready for giving, where there are many marks of enjoyment.

sanskrit: gi̱rīm̐r ajrā̱n reja̍mānām̐ adhāraya̱d dyauḥ kra̍ndad a̱ntari̍kṣāṇi kopayat | sa̱mī̱cī̱ne dhi̱ṣaṇe̱ vi ṣka̍bhāyati̱ vṛṣṇa̍ḥ pī̱tvā mada̍ u̱kthāni̍ śaṁsati ||
english: He held up the trembling hills and open plains; heaven roared and the middle regions were stirred. He propped apart the two concordant spheres of thought; drunk with exhilaration, the bull recites the sacred verses.

sanskrit: i̱mam bi̍bharmi̱ sukṛ̍taṁ te aṅku̱śaṁ yenā̍ru̱jāsi̍ maghavañ chaphā̱ruja̍ḥ | a̱smin su te̱ sava̍ne astv o̱kya̍ṁ su̱ta i̱ṣṭau ma̍ghavan bo̱dhy ābha̍gaḥ ||
english: I bear for thee this well-crafted goad with which thou forcest open, O Maghavan, thou who breakest with hooves. At this pressing let it be thy home — be wakeful at the desired soma-pressing, O Maghavan, as one worthy of the share.

sanskrit: gobhi̍ṣ ṭare̱māma̍tiṁ du̱revā̱ṁ yave̍na̱ kṣudha̍m puruhūta̱ viśvā̍m | va̱yaṁ rāja̍bhiḥ pratha̱mā dhanā̍ny a̱smāke̍na vṛ̱jane̍nā jayema ||
english: With cattle may we overcome the niggardly one who is hard to approach, and with barley overcome all hunger, O much-invoked. May we, with kings, be first to win riches, with our own community winning.

sanskrit: bṛha̱spati̍r na̱ḥ pari̍ pātu pa̱ścād u̱totta̍rasmā̱d adha̍rād aghā̱yoḥ | indra̍ḥ pu̱rastā̍d u̱ta ma̍dhya̱to na̱ḥ sakhā̱ sakhi̍bhyo̱ vari̍vaḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind and from above, from below, and from the evil-doer. May Indra in front and from the midst of us, as friend to friends, make wide space for us.

sanskrit: di̱vas pari̍ pratha̱maṁ ja̍jñe a̱gnir a̱smad dvi̱tīya̱m pari̍ jā̱tave̍dāḥ | tṛ̱tīya̍m a̱psu nṛ̱maṇā̱ aja̍sra̱m indhā̍na enaṁ jarate svā̱dhīḥ ||
english: Agni was born first from heaven; secondly Jātavedas was born from us. Thirdly, [he was born] in the waters, he of manly wisdom, inexhaustible — the wise man, kindling him, worships him.

sanskrit: vi̱dmā te̍ agne tre̱dhā tra̱yāṇi̍ vi̱dmā te̱ dhāma̱ vibhṛ̍tā puru̱trā | vi̱dmā te̱ nāma̍ para̱maṁ guhā̱ yad vi̱dmā tam utsa̱ṁ yata̍ āja̱gantha̍ ||
english: O Agni, we know thy three forms in their threefold nature; we know thy dwelling-places borne in many places. We know thy supreme name which is hidden; we know the spring from which thou hast come forth.

sanskrit: sa̱mu̱dre tvā̍ nṛ̱maṇā̍ a̱psv a1̱̍ntar nṛ̱cakṣā̍ īdhe di̱vo a̍gna̱ ūdha̍n | tṛ̱tīye̍ tvā̱ raja̍si tasthi̱vāṁsa̍m a̱pām u̱pasthe̍ mahi̱ṣā a̍vardhan ||
english: O Agni, the manliness-minded one kindled thee in the sea, in the waters within; the man-seeing one [kindled thee] at the udder of heaven. Standing in the third realm, in the lap of the waters, the great ones increased thee.

sanskrit: akra̍ndad a̱gniḥ sta̱naya̍nn iva̱ dyauḥ kṣāmā̱ reri̍had vī̱rudha̍ḥ sama̱ñjan | sa̱dyo ja̍jñā̱no vi hīm i̱ddho akhya̱d ā roda̍sī bhā̱nunā̍ bhāty a̱ntaḥ ||
english: Agni cried out like thundering heaven; licking the plants, he scorched the earth. Just born, kindled, he gazed all around; blazing within, he lit up both worlds with his radiance.

sanskrit: śrī̱ṇām u̍dā̱ro dha̱ruṇo̍ rayī̱ṇām ma̍nī̱ṣāṇā̱m prārpa̍ṇa̱ḥ soma̍gopāḥ | vasu̍ḥ sū̱nuḥ saha̍so a̱psu rājā̱ vi bhā̱ty agra̍ u̱ṣasā̍m idhā̱naḥ ||
english: He is the noble giver of good things, the foundation of riches, the inspirer of those who contemplate, the guardian of soma. The good son of strength, the king in the waters, blazes forth at the front of the dawns, being kindled.

sanskrit: viśva̍sya ke̱tur bhuva̍nasya̱ garbha̱ ā roda̍sī apṛṇā̱j jāya̍mānaḥ | vī̱ḻuṁ ci̱d adri̍m abhinat parā̱yañ janā̱ yad a̱gnim aya̍janta̱ pañca̍ ||
english: The flag of all things, the embryo of the world — being born, he filled both world-halves. He even clove the firm rock as he went forth, when the five peoples worshipped Agni.

sanskrit: u̱śik pā̍va̱ko a̍ra̱tiḥ su̍me̱dhā marte̍ṣv a̱gnir a̱mṛto̱ ni dhā̍yi | iya̍rti dhū̱mam a̍ru̱ṣam bhari̍bhra̱d uc chu̱kreṇa̍ śo̱ciṣā̱ dyām ina̍kṣan ||
english: Eager, purifying, incessant, of good wisdom — Agni, the immortal, was implanted among mortals. Carrying it, he sends the ruddy smoke upward, reaching to the sky with his brilliant flame.

sanskrit: dṛ̱śā̱no ru̱kma u̍rvi̱yā vy a̍dyaud du̱rmarṣa̱m āyu̍ḥ śri̱ye ru̍cā̱naḥ | a̱gnir a̱mṛto̍ abhava̱d vayo̍bhi̱r yad e̍na̱ṁ dyaur ja̱naya̍t su̱retā̍ḥ ||
english: The golden ornament, seen afar, blazed wide; shining with glory, his life is hard to endure. Agni became immortal with his forms, when heaven, of good seed, begat him.

sanskrit: yas te̍ a̱dya kṛ̱ṇava̍d bhadraśoce 'pū̱paṁ de̍va ghṛ̱tava̍ntam agne | pra taṁ na̍ya prata̱raṁ vasyo̱ acchā̱bhi su̱mnaṁ de̱vabha̍ktaṁ yaviṣṭha ||
english: He who makes for thee today, O Agni of auspicious flame, a ghee-laden sacrificial cake, O god — lead him onward to better and better fortune; grant him the divine favour, O youngest one.

sanskrit: ā tam bha̍ja sauśrava̱seṣv a̍gna u̱ktha-u̍ktha̱ ā bha̍ja śa̱syamā̍ne | pri̱yaḥ sūrye̍ pri̱yo a̱gnā bha̍vā̱ty uj jā̱tena̍ bhi̱nada̱d uj jani̍tvaiḥ ||
english: O Agni, give him a share in the [wealth won through] glorious praise; give him a share at each recitation of lauds. He becomes dear to Sūrya, dear to Agni; let him burst forth with what is born, burst forth with successive generations.

sanskrit: tvām a̍gne̱ yaja̍mānā̱ anu̱ dyūn viśvā̱ vasu̍ dadhire̱ vāryā̍ṇi | tvayā̍ sa̱ha dravi̍ṇam i̱cchamā̍nā vra̱jaṁ goma̍ntam u̱śijo̱ vi va̍vruḥ ||
english: Thee, O Agni, the sacrificers have held as all desirable goods through the days. Seeking riches together with thee, the eager worshippers have opened up the cow-pen.

sanskrit: astā̍vy a̱gnir na̱rāṁ su̱śevo̍ vaiśvāna̱ra ṛṣi̍bhi̱ḥ soma̍gopāḥ | a̱dve̱ṣe dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī hu̍vema̱ devā̍ dha̱tta ra̱yim a̱sme su̱vīra̍m ||
english: Agni Vaiśvānara, the guardian of soma, beloved of men, has been praised by the seers. With benevolence may we call on Heaven and Earth; O gods, grant us riches together with good heroes.

sanskrit: pra hotā̍ jā̱to ma̱hān na̍bho̱vin nṛ̱ṣadvā̍ sīdad a̱pām u̱pasthe̍ | dadhi̱r yo dhāyi̱ sa te̱ vayā̍ṁsi ya̱ntā vasū̍ni vidha̱te ta̍nū̱pāḥ ||
english: The great Hotṛ priest, born like the cloud-born one, the man-seated one, has settled in the lap of the waters. He who was made the firm-upheld one — he, protecting the body, as the guide of riches for the worshipper, branches forth.

sanskrit: i̱maṁ vi̱dhanto̍ a̱pāṁ sa̱dhasthe̍ pa̱śuṁ na na̱ṣṭam pa̱dair anu̍ gman | guhā̱ cata̍ntam u̱śijo̱ namo̍bhir i̱cchanto̱ dhīrā̱ bhṛga̍vo 'vindan ||
english: Worshipping him in the dwelling-place of the waters, they followed [him] by his tracks like a lost animal. The wise Bhṛgus, seeking with reverence, found him who was lurking in the secret place.

sanskrit: i̱maṁ tri̱to bhūry a̍vindad i̱cchan vai̍bhūva̱so mū̱rdhany aghnyā̍yāḥ | sa śevṛ̍dho jā̱ta ā ha̱rmyeṣu̱ nābhi̱r yuvā̍ bhavati roca̱nasya̍ ||
english: Trita, eagerly seeking, found him abundantly at the top of the inexhaustible Vaibhūvasa. Born to growth in the houses, the young one becomes the navel of the shining realm.

sanskrit: ma̱ndraṁ hotā̍ram u̱śijo̱ namo̍bhi̱ḥ prāñca̍ṁ ya̱jñaṁ ne̱tāra̍m adhva̱rāṇā̍m | vi̱śām a̍kṛṇvann ara̱tim pā̍va̱kaṁ ha̍vya̱vāha̱ṁ dadha̍to̱ mānu̍ṣeṣu ||
english: The eager ones have set up with their reverences the gladdening Hotṛ, the forward-leading priest, the guide of rites; they made the purifying, oblation-carrying Arāti into the priest of the clans, establishing him among humans.

sanskrit: pra bhū̱r jaya̍ntam ma̱hāṁ vi̍po̱dhām mū̱rā amū̍ram pu̱rāṁ da̱rmāṇa̍m | naya̍nto̱ garbha̍ṁ va̱nāṁ dhiya̍ṁ dhu̱r hiri̍śmaśru̱ṁ nārvā̍ṇa̱ṁ dhana̍rcam ||
english: The great one arose victorious, the far-inspiring one, who destroys fortresses, though without intellect of his own — those guiding the embryo of the forests have placed the inspired thought; golden-bearded, swift as a horse, rich in wealth he blazes.

sanskrit: ni pa̱styā̍su tri̱taḥ sta̍bhū̱yan pari̍vīto̱ yonau̍ sīdad a̱ntaḥ | ata̍ḥ sa̱ṁgṛbhyā̍ vi̱śāṁ damū̍nā̱ vidha̍rmaṇāya̱ntrair ī̍yate̱ nṝn ||
english: Trita, supporting [himself] in the dwelling-places, enveloped, settled inward in the womb. Taking from there, the house-master of the clans is led without restraint to men with his holding of the law.

sanskrit: a̱syājarā̍so da̱mām a̱ritrā̍ a̱rcaddhū̍māso a̱gnaya̍ḥ pāva̱kāḥ | śvi̱tī̱caya̍ḥ śvā̱trāso̍ bhura̱ṇyavo̍ vana̱rṣado̍ vā̱yavo̱ na somā̍ḥ ||
english: His unaging flames are the oarsmen of the house; the purifying fires blaze with luminous smoke. White-gleaming, surging, active, dwelling in the forest — like soma-draughts, like winds they move.

sanskrit: pra ji̱hvayā̍ bharate̱ vepo̍ a̱gniḥ pra va̱yunā̍ni̱ ceta̍sā pṛthi̱vyāḥ ||
english: Agni carries forth the trembling flame with his tongue; with his mind he carries forth the marks of the earth. They who are purifying — the Āyavas set up the gladdening Hotṛ, the most worthy of worship, as most fit for sacrifice.

sanskrit: dyāvā̱ yam a̱gnim pṛ̍thi̱vī jani̍ṣṭā̱m āpa̱s tvaṣṭā̱ bhṛga̍vo̱ yaṁ saho̍bhiḥ | ī̱ḻenya̍m pratha̱mam mā̍ta̱riśvā̍ de̱vās ta̍takṣu̱r mana̍ve̱ yaja̍tram ||
english: The Agni whom Heaven and Earth brought forth, whom the Waters, Tvaṣṭṛ, and the Bhṛgus brought forth with their powers — Mātariśvan first made the adorable one to be praised; the gods fashioned him as the adorable one for Manu.

sanskrit: yaṁ tvā̍ de̱vā da̍dhi̱re ha̍vya̱vāha̍m puru̱spṛho̱ mānu̍ṣāso̱ yaja̍tram | sa yāma̍nn agne stuva̱te vayo̍ dhā̱ḥ pra de̍va̱yan ya̱śasa̱ḥ saṁ hi pū̱rvīḥ ||
english: Thee whom the gods established as oblation-carrier, the adorable one desired by many humans — thee, O Agni, as thou goest, thou givest sustenance to the praising one; moving god-ward, thou dost bring together many glories.

sanskrit: ja̱gṛ̱bhmā te̱ dakṣi̍ṇam indra̱ hasta̍ṁ vasū̱yavo̍ vasupate̱ vasū̍nām | vi̱dmā hi tvā̱ gopa̍tiṁ śūra̱ gonā̍m a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: We, desiring wealth, have grasped thy right hand, O Indra, O lord of riches. For we know thee as the bull-hero, the guardian of the cows — give us a brilliant, virile wealth.

sanskrit: svā̱yu̱dhaṁ svava̍saṁ sunī̱thaṁ catu̍ḥsamudraṁ dha̱ruṇa̍ṁ rayī̱ṇām | ca̱rkṛtya̱ṁ śaṁsya̱m bhūri̍vāram a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: Give us a brilliant, virile wealth — well-weaponed, well-housed, well-guided, four-oceaned, the steadfast foundation of riches — active, praiseworthy, of many gifts.

sanskrit: su̱brahmā̍ṇaṁ de̱vava̍ntam bṛ̱hanta̍m u̱ruṁ ga̍bhī̱ram pṛ̱thubu̍dhnam indra | śru̱taṛ̍ṣim u̱gram a̍bhimāti̱ṣāha̍m a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: O Indra, give us a brilliant, virile wealth — well-brahmanic, accompanied by the gods, great, wide, deep, of broad base, of renowned wisdom, terrible, overwhelming adversaries.

sanskrit: sa̱nadvā̍ja̱ṁ vipra̍vīra̱ṁ taru̍traṁ dhana̱spṛta̍ṁ śūśu̱vāṁsa̍ṁ su̱dakṣa̍m | da̱syu̱hana̍m pū̱rbhida̍m indra sa̱tyam a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: O Indra, give us a brilliant, virile wealth — ever prize-winning, inspiredly heroic, overcoming, touching riches, swelling with growth, of good skill, truly slaying the Dasyus, breaking through the fortresses.

sanskrit: aśvā̍vantaṁ ra̱thina̍ṁ vī̱rava̍ntaṁ saha̱sriṇa̍ṁ śa̱tina̱ṁ vāja̍m indra | bha̱dravrā̍ta̱ṁ vipra̍vīraṁ sva̱rṣām a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: O Indra, give us a brilliant, virile wealth — rich in horses, furnished with chariots, rich in heroes, of a thousand, a hundred contests, of auspicious vow, inspiredly heroic, winning the sun.

sanskrit: pra sa̱ptagu̍m ṛ̱tadhī̍tiṁ sume̱dhām bṛha̱spati̍m ma̱tir acchā̍ jigāti | ya ā̍ṅgira̱so nama̍sopa̱sadyo̱ 'smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: The prayer goes forth toward Bṛhaspati of the seven tones, the one whose thought is true, of good wisdom — he who is of the Aṅgiras clan, approachable with reverence — may he give us a brilliant, virile wealth.

sanskrit: vanī̍vāno̱ mama̍ dū̱tāsa̱ indra̱ṁ stomā̍ś caranti suma̱tīr i̍yā̱nāḥ | hṛ̱di̱spṛśo̱ mana̍sā va̱cyamā̍nā a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: My lauds, imploring, moving as my messengers, seeking good favour, travel toward Indra — touching the heart, being spoken with the mind; may he give us a brilliant, virile wealth.

sanskrit: yat tvā̱ yāmi̍ da̱ddhi tan na̍ indra bṛ̱hanta̱ṁ kṣaya̱m asa̍ma̱ṁ janā̍nām | a̱bhi tad dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī gṛ̍ṇītām a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
english: What I seek from thee, O Indra, grant us that — the great, unequalled dwelling for the peoples. Let Heaven and Earth speak in agreement with this; give us a brilliant, virile wealth.

sanskrit: a̱ham bhu̍va̱ṁ vasu̍naḥ pū̱rvyas pati̍r a̱haṁ dhanā̍ni̱ saṁ ja̍yāmi̱ śaśva̍taḥ | māṁ ha̍vante pi̱tara̱ṁ na ja̱ntavo̱ 'haṁ dā̱śuṣe̱ vi bha̍jāmi̱ bhoja̍nam ||
english: I was the first lord of riches; I win wealth perpetually. Living creatures call on me as on a father; I apportion enjoyment to the pious worshipper.

sanskrit: a̱ham indro̱ rodho̱ vakṣo̱ atha̍rvaṇas tri̱tāya̱ gā a̍janaya̱m ahe̱r adhi̍ | a̱haṁ dasyu̍bhya̱ḥ pari̍ nṛ̱mṇam ā da̍de go̱trā śikṣa̍n dadhī̱ce mā̍ta̱riśva̍ne ||
english: I, Indra, having raised the obstruction and nurtured the Atharvan, produced the cows upon the serpent for Trita. I seize the manly power away from the Dasyus; teaching the cow-pen, [I give] to Dadhīca and Mātariśvan.

sanskrit: mahya̱ṁ tvaṣṭā̱ vajra̍m atakṣad āya̱sam mayi̍ de̱vāso̍ 'vṛja̱nn api̱ kratu̍m | mamānī̍ka̱ṁ sūrya̍syeva du̱ṣṭara̱m mām ārya̍nti kṛ̱tena̱ kartve̍na ca ||
english: For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron bolt; in me the gods have bent their will. My face is hard to endure like that of the sun; people approach me with what has been done and what is to be done.

sanskrit: a̱ham e̱taṁ ga̱vyaya̱m aśvya̍m pa̱śum pu̍rī̱ṣiṇa̱ṁ sāya̍kenā hira̱ṇyaya̍m | pu̱rū sa̱hasrā̱ ni śi̍śāmi dā̱śuṣe̱ yan mā̱ somā̍sa u̱kthino̱ ama̍ndiṣuḥ ||
english: I sharpen this cattle-winning, horse-winning animal — the one rich in food, golden, with an arrow-swift [movement] — many thousands [I give] to the worshipper, when the soma-draughts with their lauds have gladdened me.

sanskrit: a̱ham indro̱ na parā̍ jigya̱ id dhana̱ṁ na mṛ̱tyave 'va̍ tasthe̱ kadā̍ ca̱na | soma̱m in mā̍ su̱nvanto̍ yācatā̱ vasu̱ na me̍ pūravaḥ sa̱khye ri̍ṣāthana ||
english: I, Indra, have never lost the prize; I have never yielded to death at any time. Press soma and ask me for riches; O Pūrus, do not fall into ruin in my friendship.

sanskrit: a̱ham e̱tāñ chāśva̍sato̱ dvā-dvendra̱ṁ ye vajra̍ṁ yu̱dhaye 'kṛ̍ṇvata | ā̱hvaya̍mānā̱m̐ ava̱ hanma̍nāhanaṁ dṛ̱ḻhā vada̱nn ana̍masyur nama̱svina̍ḥ ||
english: I smote one by one these two who were ever hostile, who armed the bolt against Indra in battle. Those who were calling out I struck down with my blow; speaking firm [words], those who did not bow I made to bow.

sanskrit: a̱bhī̱3̱̍dam eka̱m eko̍ asmi ni̱ṣṣāḻ a̱bhī dvā kim u̱ traya̍ḥ karanti | khale̱ na pa̱rṣān prati̍ hanmi̱ bhūri̱ kim mā̍ nindanti̱ śatra̍vo 'ni̱ndrāḥ ||
english: I alone am prepared to face one; what then can two, or three, do? I strike many back like heaps of chaff on a threshing floor. Why do my foes who are without Indra blame me?

sanskrit: a̱haṁ gu̱ṅgubhyo̍ atithi̱gvam iṣka̍ra̱m iṣa̱ṁ na vṛ̍tra̱tura̍ṁ vi̱kṣu dhā̍rayam | yat pa̍rṇaya̱ghna u̱ta vā̍ karañja̱he prāham ma̱he vṛ̍tra̱hatye̱ aśu̍śravi ||
english: I extricated Atithigva from the Guṅgus; I sustained nourishment like a Vṛtra-slayer among the clans. When [battle raged] around Parṇayaghna and around Karañja — there I was heard in the great Vṛtra-slaying.

sanskrit: pra me̱ namī̍ sā̱pya i̱ṣe bhu̱je bhū̱d gavā̱m eṣe̍ sa̱khyā kṛ̍ṇuta dvi̱tā | di̱dyuṁ yad a̍sya sami̱theṣu̍ ma̱ṁhaya̱m ād id e̍na̱ṁ śaṁsya̍m u̱kthya̍ṁ karam ||
english: Namī Sāpya has come forward to my aid for nourishment and enjoyment; establish friendship twofold through the pursuit of cattle. When I enkindled the lightning in battles for him, then I made him worthy of praise and of laud.

sanskrit: pra nema̍smin dadṛśe̱ somo̍ a̱ntar go̱pā nema̍m ā̱vir a̱sthā kṛ̍ṇoti | sa ti̱gmaśṛ̍ṅgaṁ vṛṣa̱bhaṁ yuyu̍tsan dru̱has ta̍sthau bahu̱le ba̱ddho a̱ntaḥ ||
english: Soma has been seen within this [one], half of it; as guardian he makes half manifest. Wishing to battle the bull with the sharp horn, [the demon] stood waiting for treachery, bound deeply within.

sanskrit: ā̱di̱tyānā̱ṁ vasū̍nāṁ ru̱driyā̍ṇāṁ de̱vo de̱vānā̱ṁ na mi̍nāmi̱ dhāma̍ | te mā̍ bha̱drāya̱ śava̍se tatakṣu̱r apa̍rājita̱m astṛ̍ta̱m aṣā̍ḻham ||
english: Of the Ādityas, of the Vasus, of the Rudras, I as god do not diminish the ordinance of the gods. They have fashioned me for auspicious power — unconquered, uncast down, invincible.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ dā̍ṁ gṛṇa̱te pūrvya̱ṁ vasv a̱ham brahma̍ kṛṇava̱m mahya̱ṁ vardha̍nam | a̱ham bhu̍va̱ṁ yaja̍mānasya codi̱tāya̍jvanaḥ sākṣi̱ viśva̍smi̱n bhare̍ ||
english: I give the ancient good to the singer; I make the prayer that is my own growth. I became the impeller of the sacrificer; I am the witness of the non-sacrificer in every contest.

sanskrit: māṁ dhu̱r indra̱ṁ nāma̍ de̱vatā̍ di̱vaś ca̱ gmaś cā̱pāṁ ca̍ ja̱ntava̍ḥ | a̱haṁ harī̱ vṛṣa̍ṇā̱ vivra̍tā ra̱ghū a̱haṁ vajra̱ṁ śava̍se dhṛ̱ṣṇv ā da̍de ||
english: They have made me Indra by name as the divine power; the beings of heaven, of earth, and of the waters [know me thus]. I hold the two bay stallions, swift of diverse courses; I boldly take up the bolt for might.

sanskrit: a̱ham atka̍ṁ ka̱vaye̍ śiśnatha̱ṁ hathai̍r a̱haṁ kutsa̍m āvam ā̱bhir ū̱tibhi̍ḥ | a̱haṁ śuṣṇa̍sya̱ śnathi̍tā̱ vadha̍r yama̱ṁ na yo ra̱ra ārya̱ṁ nāma̱ dasya̍ve ||
english: With my blows I shattered the mantle for the sage; I assisted Kutsa with these aids. I am the slayer of Śuṣṇa, the restraining weapon — one who never gave the noble name to the Dasyu.

sanskrit: a̱ham pi̱teva̍ veta̱sūm̐r a̱bhiṣṭa̍ye̱ tugra̱ṁ kutsā̍ya̱ smadi̍bhaṁ ca randhayam | a̱ham bhu̍va̱ṁ yaja̍mānasya rā̱jani̱ pra yad bhare̱ tuja̍ye̱ na pri̱yādhṛṣe̍ ||
english: Like a father I subdued the Vetasus for conquest; I subdued Tugra and Smadibha for Kutsa. I became the king of the sacrificer when I press forward in battle against the dear untouchable enemy.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ ra̍ndhaya̱m mṛga̍yaṁ śru̱tarva̍ṇe̱ yan māji̍hīta va̱yunā̍ ca̱nānu̱ṣak | a̱haṁ ve̱śaṁ na̱mram ā̱yave̍ 'karam a̱haṁ savyā̍ya̱ paḍgṛ̍bhim arandhayam ||
english: I subdued the deer-slayer Mṛgaya for Śrutarvaṇa, who hurled himself [against me] without even following a sign. I made the obedient Veśa for Āyu; I subdued the hexapod Padgṛbhi for Savya.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ sa yo nava̍vāstvam bṛ̱hadra̍tha̱ṁ saṁ vṛ̱treva̱ dāsa̍ṁ vṛtra̱hāru̍jam | yad va̱rdhaya̍ntam pra̱thaya̍ntam ānu̱ṣag dū̱re pā̱re raja̍so roca̱nāka̍ram ||
english: I am the one who crushed the Dāsa Navavāstava with the great chariot, shattering him like Vṛtra, the Vṛtra-slaying smasher — him who was growing and spreading continuously, who had made a glittering place at the far end of the realm.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ sūrya̍sya̱ pari̍ yāmy ā̱śubhi̱ḥ praita̱śebhi̱r vaha̍māna̱ oja̍sā | yan mā̍ sā̱vo manu̍ṣa̱ āha̍ ni̱rṇija̱ ṛdha̍k kṛṣe̱ dāsa̱ṁ kṛtvya̱ṁ hathai̍ḥ ||
english: I go around the sun with my swift [horses], the Pra-Etaśas, being carried with might. When the human champion called me the shining, clearly victorious one — with my blows I made a Dāsa of the villain.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ sa̍pta̱hā nahu̍ṣo̱ nahu̍ṣṭara̱ḥ prāśrā̍vaya̱ṁ śava̍sā tu̱rvaśa̱ṁ yadu̍m | a̱haṁ ny a1̱̍nyaṁ saha̍sā̱ saha̍s kara̱ṁ nava̱ vrādha̍to nava̱tiṁ ca̍ vakṣayam ||
english: I, the slayer of seven, mightier than Nahuṣa, caused Turvaśa and Yadu to be heard by my power. I, with might overpowering might, caused to decrease nine and ninety of the weakened ones, subduing the others.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ sa̱pta sra̱vato̍ dhāraya̱ṁ vṛṣā̍ dravi̱tnva̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyāṁ sī̱rā adhi̍ | a̱ham arṇā̍ṁsi̱ vi ti̍rāmi su̱kratu̍r yu̱dhā vi̍da̱m mana̍ve gā̱tum i̱ṣṭaye̍ ||
english: I, the bull, the fast-moving one, held the seven streams as ploughs upon the earth. I, of excellent resolve, cross through the floods; I found through battle the way to the sun for Manu, for the sacrifice.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ tad ā̍su dhāraya̱ṁ yad ā̍su̱ na de̱vaś ca̱na tvaṣṭādhā̍raya̱d ruśa̍t | spā̱rhaṁ gavā̱m ūdha̍ḥsu va̱kṣaṇā̱sv ā madho̱r madhu̱ śvātrya̱ṁ soma̍m ā̱śira̍m ||
english: I held therein what even the god Tvaṣṭṛ could not hold as shining — the desirable, mixed soma with the honey of honey in the udders of cows, in their bellies, the Śvātra soma.

sanskrit: e̱vā de̱vām̐ indro̍ vivye̱ nṝn pra cyau̱tnena̍ ma̱ghavā̍ sa̱tyarā̍dhāḥ | viśvet tā te̍ harivaḥ śacīvo̱ 'bhi tu̱rāsa̍ḥ svayaśo gṛṇanti ||
english: Thus Indra, whose bounty is true, has encompassed the gods and men with his impulse, the Bountiful One. All these feats of thine, O lord of the bay steeds, O mighty one — swift heroes of their own renown declare them.

sanskrit: pra vo̍ ma̱he manda̍mānā̱yāndha̱so 'rcā̍ vi̱śvāna̍rāya viśvā̱bhuve̍ | indra̍sya̱ yasya̱ suma̍kha̱ṁ saho̱ mahi̱ śravo̍ nṛ̱mṇaṁ ca̱ roda̍sī sapa̱ryata̍ḥ ||
english: Sing forth with laud to the great one who exhilarates himself with the soma-drink, to the all-human, the all-being Indra — whose fair-jawed might, whose great glory and manly power the two worlds serve.

sanskrit: so ci̱n nu sakhyā̱ narya̍ i̱naḥ stu̱taś ca̱rkṛtya̱ indro̱ māva̍te̱ nare̍ | viśvā̍su dhū̱rṣu vā̍ja̱kṛtye̍ṣu satpate vṛ̱tre vā̱psv a1̱̍bhi śū̍ra mandase ||
english: He truly, the manly Indra, mighty through friendship, ever-active, praised, exhilarates himself for the pious man. In all charges, in prize-winning actions, at Vṛtra, in the waters, thou rejoicest, O hero, O lord of the good.

sanskrit: ke te nara̍ indra̱ ye ta̍ i̱ṣe ye te̍ su̱mnaṁ sa̍dha̱nya1̱̍m iya̍kṣān | ke te̱ vājā̍yāsu̱ryā̍ya hinvire̱ ke a̱psu svāsū̱rvarā̍su̱ pauṁsye̍ ||
english: Who are thy men, O Indra, who desire thy bounty? Who would honor thy auspicious shared goodwill? Who would urge thee for prize and for lordly power? Who [would urge thee] in the waters, in fair regions, in virile might?

sanskrit: bhuva̱s tvam i̍ndra̱ brahma̍ṇā ma̱hān bhuvo̱ viśve̍ṣu̱ sava̍neṣu ya̱jñiya̍ḥ | bhuvo̱ nṝm̐ś cyau̱tno viśva̍smi̱n bhare̱ jyeṣṭha̍ś ca̱ mantro̍ viśvacarṣaṇe ||
english: Thou hast become great through the sacred formulation, O Indra; thou hast become the one worthy of worship at all soma-pressings. Thou hast become the impeller of men in every contest; the foremost prayer, O one seen by all.

sanskrit: avā̱ nu ka̱ṁ jyāyā̍n ya̱jñava̍naso ma̱hīṁ ta̱ omā̍trāṁ kṛ̱ṣṭayo̍ viduḥ | aso̱ nu ka̍m a̱jaro̱ vardhā̍ś ca̱ viśved e̱tā sava̍nā tūtu̱mā kṛ̍ṣe ||
english: Who then is greater than thee who lovest the sacrifice? The peoples know thy great protection. Mayest thou be truly unaging and growing, winning all these soma-pressings, O industrious one.

sanskrit: e̱tā viśvā̱ sava̍nā tūtu̱mā kṛ̍ṣe sva̱yaṁ sū̍no sahaso̱ yāni̍ dadhi̱ṣe | varā̍ya te̱ pātra̱ṁ dharma̍ṇe̱ tanā̍ ya̱jño mantro̱ brahmodya̍ta̱ṁ vaca̍ḥ ||
english: Win all these soma-pressings by thine own power, O Son of Strength, thou who holdest them. For thy choosing, the vessel [is set], by the sacred ordinance perpetuated; the sacrifice, the sacred formula, the brahman speech held upraised.

sanskrit: ye te̍ vipra brahma̱kṛta̍ḥ su̱te sacā̱ vasū̍nāṁ ca̱ vasu̍naś ca dā̱vane̍ | pra te su̱mnasya̱ mana̍sā pa̱thā bhu̍va̱n made̍ su̱tasya̍ so̱myasyāndha̍saḥ ||
english: The inspired ones who are made brahmanic by thee are present at the pressing — for giving of riches and of goods. May they go forth on the path of thy goodwill through mind, in the exhilaration of the pressed soma-drink.
